9
A rock R of mass 1.0  1027
kg is a large distance from a star S and is travelling at a speed of
1.0  104
m s–1. The star has mass 1.0  1030
kg. The rock travels around the star on the path
shown so that it reverses its direction of motion and, when finally again a large distance from the
star, has the same speed as initially.
R
mass 1.0  1027 kg
X
S
mass 1.0  1030 kg
speed 1.0  104 m s–1
speed 1.0  104 m s–1
Which statement is correct?
A
The change in the momentum of S is in the direction of arrow X.
B
The change in the velocity of S is approximately 20 m s–1.
C
The magnitude of the change of momentum of R is 103 times greater than the magnitude of
the change of momentum of S.
D
The momentum of R does not change.

hints: Notice the rock enters moving to the right at $1.0 \times 10^{4} \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and leaves moving to the left at the same speed, so treat momentum as a vector.
Recall that the isolated R plus S system conserves total momentum, so $\Delta p_S = -\Delta p_R$ in both magnitude and direction.
Calculate the magnitude $\lvert \Delta p_R \rvert = m\lvert v_{final} - v_{initial} \rvert$ for the reversal, then divide by the star mass $1.0 \times 10^{30} \text{ kg}$ to find its velocity change.
walkthrough: Take right as positive. Initial momentum of R is $p_i = +m_R v$ and final momentum is $p_f = -m_R v$ with $m_R = 1.0 \times 10^{27} \text{ kg}$ and $v = 1.0 \times 10^{4} \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Change of momentum of R is $\Delta p_R = p_f - p_i = -2m_R v = -2.0 \times 10^{31} \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, so its magnitude is $2.0 \times 10^{31} \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ directed to the left.
For the isolated system total momentum is conserved, so $\Delta p_S + \Delta p_R = 0$ and $\Delta p_S = +2.0 \times 10^{31} \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ directed to the right, opposite to arrow X.
Convert this to velocity change of the star: $\Delta v_S = \lvert \Delta p_S \rvert / M_S$ with $M_S = 1.0 \times 10^{30} \text{ kg}$.
Substitution gives $\Delta v_S = 2.0 \times 10^{31} / 1.0 \times 10^{30} = 20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, with units of velocity. This is option B.

A.explanation: The rock gains momentum to the left, so the star must gain equal momentum to the right to conserve total momentum, which is opposite to arrow X.

B.explanation: The star gains momentum of magnitude $2.0 \times 10^{31} \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, giving $\Delta v = \Delta p/M \approx 20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: Total momentum is conserved, so the magnitudes of the changes of momentum of R and S are equal, not different by $10^3$.

D.explanation: Speed is unchanged but direction reverses from right to left, so the vector momentum $p = mv$ changes by $2mv$.
